messages:
Nora (sales): ACME POC blocked — their staging app can't reach our private endpoint from one AZ. They reported TLS cert mismatch + DNS NXDOMAIN from app nodes. Can we triage quickly? :wave:

ACME-Security: Confirmed. From app-az2 we get NXDOMAIN for private.redwood-acme.internal and from app-az1 we get cert "corp-inspect.local". Curl and dig logs below.

ACME-Security: ```dig @10.0.0.5 private.redwood-acme.internal +short
;; -> no output (NXDOMAIN)

curl -v https://private.redwood-acme.internal/health
* Connected to 10.4.5.6 port 443
* TLS alert, unknown CA
* SSL: certificate subject name 'corp-inspect.local' does not match target host name 'private.redwood-acme.internal'```

Kai (neteng): Two independent issues likely: DNS (hosted zone not associated with that VPC or resolver rules) and TLS inspection on egress path for the AZ that hits the corporate proxy. Which AZ maps to which egress path?

ACME-Security: az1 -> direct NAT (works), az2 -> transit + inspection appliance (fails DNS + MITM). We use a shared resolver in mgmt VPC; app VPC shouldn't be automatically able to resolve private zones unless associated.

Omar (solutions): Quick POC workarounds: 1) give ACME a public-but-restricted hostname we control + ALB IP and ask them to allow outbound to that IP for demo; 2) request they associate the private hosted zone with app VPC (security review); 3) provide a bypass IP so inspection doesn't MITM (single /32). For immediate demo, option 1 or 3 is fastest. Thoughts?

Yuki (eng-platform): We can spin a short-lived ALB with SAN covering private.redwood-acme.internal and a public IP 198.51.100.77. That avoids changing their hosted zones and keeps TLS valid. We'll restrict SG to ACME prefixes. Provision time ~25m.

ACME-Security: We prefer option 3 (bypass) for minimal firewall changes. But bypass requires change control. If you provide IP, we can add a single bypass rule for 24 hours. Provide rollback plan and cert notes.

Omar (solutions): Sounds good. If bypass is slow, fallback is the ALB approach. Action items: @ACME-Security add bypass for the /32 once we share IP. @Yuki provide IP and cert plan. @Kai validate DNS: confirm hosted zone associations so we fix root cause next week.

Yuki (eng-platform): Assigned IP 198.51.100.77. We'll terminate TLS there with cert matching the private hostname. We'll revoke the cert and remove IP after 24h. deploy-bot: queued create-poc-alb(198.51.100.77) -> in_progress.

Kai (neteng): On DNS: hosted zone "private.redwood-acme.internal" is associated only with vpc-mgmt-01. App VPC not associated. That explains NXDOMAIN. Long-term fix: either associate the zone or create a resolver inbound endpoint + rule.

ACME-Security: Bypass rule added for 198.51.100.77/32 for 24 hours. Pinged change control with rollback time. Testing now...

ACME-Security: ```curl -v https://private.redwood-acme.internal/health
* Connected to 198.51.100.77 port 443
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "status": "ok" }```

Nora (sales): Demo unblocked. Please follow up with ACME docs for the permanent fix and a note on why the hosted zone association matters. Also capture the security checklist for bypass events.

Omar (solutions): Will create a short runbook: 1) map hosted zone associations, 2) recommend resolver endpoint for cross-VPC queries, 3) note when bypass or ALB is acceptable for POC and include cert rotation and rollback. I'll attach to the deal ticket.

pooled-bot: reminder: please remove temporary IP 198.51.100.77 after 24h or escalate if extension needed.

ACME-Security: Thanks team. We'll monitor and revert the bypass after the demo window.
